props.gloss_en: this one can and that one cannot -- all agree: liable
which of them is liable? Rav Chisda: the one who can
Rav Chisda: for if the one who cannot -- what is he doing?
Rav Hamnuna: [he is doing something,] for he is assisting him
[a zav] sitting on a bed with four garments under the bed's legs -- they are impure, because it cannot stand on three
R' Shimon declares [the garments under the bed] pure
riding on an animal with four garments under the animal's legs -- they are pure, because it can stand on three
a zav lying on five benches or five money belts: lengthwise -- impure; widthwise -- pure; asleep, in doubt whether he turned over on them -- impure
R' Yosei: the horse renders impure by its forelegs, for a horse leans on its forelegs
R' Yosei: the donkey -- by its hind legs, for a donkey leans on its hind legs
R' Eliezer: one foot on a vessel (or a stone) and one on the floor -- if, were the vessel or stone removed, he could stand on one foot, his service is valid
R' Eliezer: and if not, his service is invalid
he received [the blood] in the right hand and the left assisted it -- his service is valid
